beads.name: hourly_examples
beads.explains: Turn each target hour into 12 predictors: yesterday, last week, yesterday's summary, and calendar.
beads.title: Build 12 Inputs per Hour
beads.source:
@bead("hourly_examples", strand="ridge", after=("complete_days",),
      title="Build 12 Inputs per Hour",
      io=("complete days", "(76,032, 12) hourly"),
      tokens=("12 features", "51,552", "17,256", "7,224", "lags", "calendar", "sine cosine"),
      explains="Turn each target hour into 12 predictors: yesterday, last week, yesterday's summary, and calendar.")
def hourly_examples(daily: pd.DataFrame) -> HourlyExamples:
    dates = daily.index
    yesterday = dates - pd.Timedelta(days=1)
    last_week = dates - pd.Timedelta(days=7)
    valid = yesterday.isin(dates) & last_week.isin(dates)
    dates = dates[valid]
    yesterday_load = daily.loc[yesterday[valid]].to_numpy()
    week_load = daily.loc[last_week[valid]].to_numpy()
    hours = np.tile(np.arange(24), len(dates))
    target_dates = dates.repeat(24)
    hour_angle = 2 * np.pi * hours / 24
    day_of_week = target_dates.day_of_week
    dow_angle = 2 * np.pi * day_of_week / 7
    month_angle = 2 * np.pi * target_dates.month / 12
    x = np.column_stack([
        yesterday_load.ravel(), week_load.ravel(),
        yesterday_load.mean(axis=1).repeat(24), yesterday_load.max(axis=1).repeat(24),
        yesterday_load.min(axis=1).repeat(24),
        np.sin(hour_angle), np.cos(hour_angle), np.sin(dow_angle), np.cos(dow_angle),
        np.sin(month_angle), np.cos(month_angle), day_of_week >= 5,
    ])
    return HourlyExamples(x, daily.loc[dates].to_numpy().ravel(), target_dates + pd.to_timedelta(hours, unit="h"))

numbers.operation: Stack [lag_1d_h, lag_7d_h, prev_mean, prev_max, prev_min, sin/cos(hr, dow, mo), weekend]

beads.name: ridge_search
beads.explains: Fit standardized Ridge for each alpha and keep the lowest validation MAE.
beads.title: Ridge Alpha Validation Sweep
beads.source:
@bead("ridge_search", strand="ridge", after=("hourly_examples",),
      title="Ridge Alpha Validation Sweep",
      io=("train/val 12-feat", "best α = 0.1"),
      tokens=("Ridge", "alpha", "0.1", "2,294", "2,307.95", "regularization", "L2"),
      explains="Fit standardized Ridge for each alpha and keep the lowest validation MAE.")
def ridge_search(ex: HourlyExamples, alphas=ALPHAS) -> tuple[Pipeline, list[dict]]:
    train, val = ex.split("train"), ex.split("val")
    results, best, best_mae = [], None, float("inf")
    for alpha in alphas:
        model = Pipeline([("scaler", StandardScaler()), ("ridge", Ridge(alpha=alpha))]).fit(ex.x[train], ex.y[train])
        score = errors(ex.y[val], model.predict(ex.x[val]))
        results.append({"alpha": alpha, **score})
        if score["mae_mw"] < best_mae:
            best, best_mae = model, score["mae_mw"]
    return best, results

numbers.operation: Fit StandardScaler + Ridge(alpha) on 2018-2023; pick argmin validation MAE (2024-2025)

beads.name: ridge_quadratic
beads.explains: Center the scaled training data and write Ridge as f(w) = ½wᵀHw − bᵀw.
beads.title: Form Ridge Quadratic (H, b)
beads.source:
@bead("ridge_quadratic", strand="solvers", after=("ridge_reference",),
      title="Form Ridge Quadratic (H, b)",
      io=("scaled train (12)", "H(12×12), b(12)"),
      tokens=("quadratic", "Hessian", "convex", "Ridge", "f(w)"),
      explains="Center the scaled training data and write Ridge as f(w) = ½wᵀHw − bᵀw.")
def ridge_quadratic(ex: HourlyExamples, problem: ScaledProblem) -> Quadratic:
    train = ex.split("train")
    mean_x, mean_y = problem.scaled[train].mean(axis=0), ex.y[train].mean()
    centered_x, centered_y = problem.scaled[train] - mean_x, ex.y[train] - mean_y
    n, d = centered_x.shape
    alpha = problem.reference.alpha
    hessian = (centered_x.T @ centered_x + alpha * np.eye(d)) / n
    return Quadratic(hessian, (centered_x.T @ centered_y) / n, mean_x, float(mean_y))

numbers.operation: H = (X^T X + 0.1·I) / n,  b = X^T y / n  ⇒  f(w) = 0.5 w^T H w - b^T w

beads.name: fixed_step_gd
beads.explains: Step against the gradient by 1/L, where L is the largest Hessian eigenvalue.
beads.title: Fixed-Step Gradient Descent
beads.source:
@bead("fixed_step_gd", strand="solvers", after=("ridge_quadratic",),
      title="Fixed-Step Gradient Descent",
      io=("H, b, step=1/L", "10,000 iters (cap)"),
      tokens=("fixed step", "gradient descent", "1/L", "eigenvalue", "10,000", "0.168 MW"),
      explains="Step against the gradient by 1/L, where L is the largest Hessian eigenvalue.")
def fixed_step_gd(q: Quadratic):
    started = perf_counter()
    weights, gradient, squared_norm, tolerance_squared = _start(q)
    step = 1 / np.linalg.eigvalsh(q.hessian)[-1]
    trace = [(perf_counter() - started, weights, np.sqrt(squared_norm), 0)]
    while squared_norm > tolerance_squared and len(trace) <= MAX_ITERATIONS:
        weights = weights - step * gradient
        gradient = q.hessian @ weights - q.rhs
        squared_norm = float(gradient @ gradient)
        trace.append((perf_counter() - started, weights, np.sqrt(squared_norm), 0))
    return trace, squared_norm <= tolerance_squared

numbers.operation: w_{k+1} = w_k - (1/L) (H w_k - b)  up to 10,000 iters

beads.name: armijo_gd
beads.explains: Try step 1, halve until the objective falls by at least 1e-4 · step · ‖∇f‖², then step.
beads.title: Armijo Backtracking GD
beads.source:
@bead("armijo_gd", strand="solvers", after=("ridge_quadratic",),
      title="Armijo Backtracking GD",
      io=("H, b, backtrack", "4,749 iters / 35.5 ms"),
      tokens=("Armijo", "backtracking", "line search", "4,749", "35.5 ms", "9,501"),
      explains="Try step 1, halve until the objective falls by at least 1e-4 · step · ‖∇f‖², then step.")
def armijo_gd(q: Quadratic):
    started = perf_counter()
    weights, gradient, squared_norm, tolerance_squared = _start(q)
    trials = 0
    trace = [(perf_counter() - started, weights, np.sqrt(squared_norm), trials)]
    while squared_norm > tolerance_squared and len(trace) <= MAX_ITERATIONS:
        step = ARMIJO_INITIAL_STEP
        curvature = float(gradient @ (q.hessian @ gradient))
        while True:  # exact objective change of a quadratic along -gradient
            trials += 1
            change = -step * squared_norm + 0.5 * step ** 2 * curvature
            if change <= -ARMIJO_SUFFICIENT_DECREASE * step * squared_norm:
                break
            step *= ARMIJO_SHRINK
        weights = weights - step * gradient
        gradient = q.hessian @ weights - q.rhs
        squared_norm = float(gradient @ gradient)
        trace.append((perf_counter() - started, weights, np.sqrt(squared_norm), trials))
    return trace, squared_norm <= tolerance_squared

numbers.operation: Halve step α ← 0.5α until quadratic decrease Δf ≤ -1e-4 α ‖∇f‖²

beads.name: conjugate_gradient
beads.explains: Move along directions that are conjugate under H, so each step never undoes an earlier one.
beads.title: Linear Conjugate Gradient
beads.source:
@bead("conjugate_gradient", strand="solvers", after=("ridge_quadratic",),
      title="Linear Conjugate Gradient",
      io=("H, b, H-conjugate", "13 iters / 0.12 ms"),
      tokens=("conjugate gradient", "CG", "13 iterations", "0.12 ms", "orthogonal", "fastest solver"),
      explains="Move along directions that are conjugate under H, so each step never undoes an earlier one.")
def conjugate_gradient(q: Quadratic):
    started = perf_counter()
    weights, gradient, squared_norm, tolerance_squared = _start(q)
    direction = -gradient
    trace = [(perf_counter() - started, weights, np.sqrt(squared_norm), 0)]
    while squared_norm > tolerance_squared and len(trace) <= MAX_ITERATIONS:
        curvature = q.hessian @ direction
        step = squared_norm / (direction @ curvature)
        weights = weights + step * direction
        gradient = q.hessian @ weights - q.rhs
        new_squared_norm = float(gradient @ gradient)
        direction = -gradient + (new_squared_norm / squared_norm) * direction
        squared_norm = new_squared_norm
        trace.append((perf_counter() - started, weights, np.sqrt(squared_norm), 0))
    return trace, squared_norm <= tolerance_squared

numbers.operation: Exact quadratic step α_k = ‖g_k‖² / (d_k^T H d_k); orthogonalize d_{k+1} under H

beads.name: shared_cohort
beads.explains: Join every model's saved test forecasts on timestamp and keep the 301 days all of them cover.
beads.title: Match 301 Test Days
beads.source:
@bead("shared_cohort", strand="evaluate", after=("ridge_search", "svr_search", "ffn_forecast", "lstm_ensemble"),
      title="Match 301 Test Days",
      io=("ML + LSTM + FFN CSVs", "301 days / 7,224 hrs"),
      tokens=("301 days", "7,224 hours", "shared cohort", "2026 test", "comparison"),
      explains="Join every model's saved test forecasts on timestamp and keep the 301 days all of them cover.")
def shared_cohort() -> pd.DataFrame:
    ml = pd.read_csv(PRELIMINARY / "ercot_ml_24hour_forecasts.csv", parse_dates=["timestamp"])
    lstm = pd.read_csv(PRELIMINARY / "lstm_outputs" / "lstm_day_ahead_forecasts.csv", parse_dates=["timestamp"])
    ffn = pd.read_csv(RESULTS / "feedforward" / "test_forecasts.csv", parse_dates=["timestamp"])
    shared = ml.merge(lstm[lstm["split"] == "test"], on="timestamp", validate="one_to_one")
    shared = shared.merge(ffn.drop(columns="actual_mw"), on="timestamp", validate="one_to_one").sort_values("timestamp")
    days = shared.groupby(shared["timestamp"].dt.normalize()).size()
    if len(days) != 301 or not (days == 24).all():
        raise ValueError("The saved exports must share 301 complete forecast days.")
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(shared["actual_load_mw"].to_numpy(), shared["actual_mw"].to_numpy())
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "timestamp": shared["timestamp"].to_numpy(), "actual": shared["actual_mw"].to_numpy(),
        "lstm": shared["lstm_mw"].to_numpy(), "ffn_sgd": shared["sgd_mw"].to_numpy(),
        "ffn_armijo": shared["armijo_mw"].to_numpy(), "ridge": shared["ridge_forecast_mw"].to_numpy(),
        "svr": shared["svr_forecast_mw"].to_numpy(), "previous_day": shared["naive_prev_day_mw"].to_numpy(),
        "previous_week": shared["naive_prev_week_mw"].to_numpy(),
    })

beads.name: dedupe
beads.explains: Collapse the eight zone rows of each hour into one system hour and audit the raw table.
beads.title: Audit & Deduplicate Zones
beads.source:
def audit_and_deduplicate(raw_csv_path: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
    """Audit raw multi-zone ERCOT CSV and deduplicate to a unique hourly system series.

    Each timestamp in `ercot_model_table.csv` appears 8 times (once per weather zone).
    This function:
      - Streams all rows once and verifies schema & expected columns.
      - Groups rows by `(timestamp, DSTFlag)` so the repeated `01:00:00` hour during
        each November Daylight Saving Time fall-back is preserved as two distinct hours
        rather than overwritten.
      - Verifies that `system_total_mw`, `source`, and `uri_flag` match identically across
        all 8 zones at each hour.
      - Averages zone weather readings per hour and imputes any remaining NaNs using
        medians computed strictly on the `train` split (2018-2023).

    Args:
        raw_csv_path: Path to `ercot_model_table.csv`.

    Returns:
        `(system_data, audit_summary)`:
          - `system_data`: dict of 77,496-element chronological arrays/lists.
          - `audit_summary`: JSON-serializable audit dictionary for reproducibility.
    """
    raw_csv_path = Path(raw_csv_path)
    if not raw_csv_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Raw dataset not found: {raw_csv_path}")

    # Running audit accumulators updated row-by-row during the single file pass
    total_rows = 0
    zone_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
    source_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
    missing_raw_by_col: Counter[str] = Counter()
    missing_raw_by_split: Counter[str] = Counter()
    uri_zone_rows = 0

    # Keyed by `(timestamp, DSTFlag)` because November fall-back repeats 01:00:00
    # once with DSTFlag=False and once with DSTFlag=True.
    hourly_records: dict[tuple[str, bool], dict[str, Any]] = {}
    ordered_keys: list[tuple[str, bool]] = []
    max_sys_spread = 0.0
    source_mismatch_count = 0
    uri_mismatch_count = 0

    with raw_csv_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        columns = tuple(reader.fieldnames or ())
        if columns != EXPECTED_COLUMNS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unexpected CSV columns: {columns} != {EXPECTED_COLUMNS}")

        for row in reader:
            total_rows += 1
            ts = row["timestamp"].strip()
            dst_flag = _parse_bool(row["DSTFlag"])
            source = row["source"].strip()
            uri_flag = _parse_bool(row["uri_flag"])
            zone = row["zone"].strip()
            sys_mw = float(row["system_total_mw"])
            load_mw = float(row["load_mw"])

            # Tally per-zone, per-source, and Winter Storm Uri row counts
            zone_counts[zone] += 1
            source_counts[source] += 1
            if uri_flag:
                uri_zone_rows += 1

            # Track raw weather missingness both globally and by chronological split
            split_lbl = assign_split(ts)
            weather_vals: dict[str, float] = {}
            for wcol in WEATHER_COLUMNS:
                val = _parse_float(row[wcol])
                weather_vals[wcol] = val
                if np.isnan(val):
                    missing_raw_by_col[wcol] += 1
                    missing_raw_by_split[f"{wcol}:{split_lbl}"] += 1

            # Create or update the deduplicated hourly bucket for this (timestamp, DSTFlag)
            key = (ts, dst_flag)
            rec = hourly_records.get(key)
            if rec is None:
                rec = {
                    "timestamp": ts,
                    "dst_flag": dst_flag,
                    "source": source,
                    "uri_flag": uri_flag,
                    "system_total_mw": sys_mw,
                    "zone_loads": {},
                    "weather_lists": {wcol: [] for wcol in WEATHER_COLUMNS},
                }
                hourly_records[key] = rec
                ordered_keys.append(key)
            else:
                # Sanity check: ensure system-wide values really are identical across all 8 zones
                spread = abs(rec["system_total_mw"] - sys_mw)
                if spread > max_sys_spread:
                    max_sys_spread = spread
                if rec["source"] != source:
                    source_mismatch_count += 1
                if rec["uri_flag"] != uri_flag:
                    uri_mismatch_count += 1

            # Store each individual zone's load and accumulate non-NaN weather values
            rec["zone_loads"][zone] = load_mw
            for wcol, val in weather_vals.items():
                if not np.isnan(val):
                    rec["weather_lists"][wcol].append(val)

    # Sort chronologically by timestamp string, placing DSTFlag=False before DSTFlag=True
    # on the 9 November fall-back nights so time flows strictly forward.
    ordered_keys.sort(key=lambda k: (k[0], k[1]))
    n_hours = len(ordered_keys)

    # Pre-allocate dense NumPy arrays for fast downstream slicing and plotting
    timestamps: list[str] = []
    dst_flags = np.zeros(n_hours, dtype=bool)
    sources: list[str] = []
    uri_flags = np.zeros(n_hours, dtype=bool)
    splits: list[str] = []
    system_total_mw = np.zeros(n_hours, dtype=np.float64)
    zone_load_sum_mw = np.zeros(n_hours, dtype=np.float64)
    zone_loads_arr = {z: np.zeros(n_hours, dtype=np.float64) for z in EXPECTED_ZONES}
    weather_mean_arr = {w: np.full(n_hours, np.nan, dtype=np.float64) for w in WEATHER_COLUMNS}

    # Count occurrences of each timestamp string (without DSTFlag) to detect fall-back pairs
    ts_only_counter: Counter[str] = Counter()
    for idx, key in enumerate(ordered_keys):
        rec = hourly_records[key]
        ts = rec["timestamp"]
        ts_only_counter[ts] += 1
        timestamps.append(ts)
        dst_flags[idx] = rec["dst_flag"]
        sources.append(rec["source"])
        uri_flags[idx] = rec["uri_flag"]
        splits.append(assign_split(ts))
        system_total_mw[idx] = rec["system_total_mw"]

        # Record each zone's hourly MW and compute their exact cross-zone sum
        zsum = 0.0
        for z in EXPECTED_ZONES:
            val = rec["zone_loads"][z]
            zone_loads_arr[z][idx] = val
            zsum += val
        zone_load_sum_mw[idx] = zsum

        # Compute system-wide cross-zone average weather for each valid variable
        for wcol in WEATHER_COLUMNS:
            vals = rec["weather_lists"][wcol]
            if vals:
                weather_mean_arr[wcol][idx] = float(np.mean(vals))

    # Leakage Control #1: Fit weather median imputation strictly on `train` hours (2018-2023)
    # so validation/test weather distributions never leak into training imputation rules.
    train_mask = np.array([s == "train" for s in splits], dtype=bool)
    weather_impute_medians: dict[str, float] = {}
    for wcol in WEATHER_COLUMNS:
        arr = weather_mean_arr[wcol]
        train_valid = arr[train_mask & ~np.isnan(arr)]
        med = float(np.median(train_valid)) if train_valid.size > 0 else 0.0
        weather_impute_medians[wcol] = med
        nan_mask = np.isnan(arr)
        if np.any(nan_mask):
            arr[nan_mask] = med

    # Identify all 9 DST fall-back repeated timestamps and any missing calendar dates
    dst_repeated_timestamps = sorted(ts for ts, cnt in ts_only_counter.items() if cnt > 1)
    missing_dates = _find_missing_dates(timestamps)

    # Summarize hourly load distributions for Train, Validation, and Test splits
    split_hour_counts = dict(Counter(splits))
    split_load_stats = {
        split_name: _summarize_load_dict(
            system_total_mw[np.array([s == split_name for s in splits], dtype=bool)],
            include_hours=True,
        )
        for split_name in ("train", "val", "test")
    }

    uri_vals = system_total_mw[uri_flags]
    uri_timestamps = [ts for ts, u in zip(timestamps, uri_flags) if u]

    # Package full machine-readable audit report
    audit_summary: dict[str, Any] = {
        "raw_file": raw_csv_path.name,
        "total_raw_rows": total_rows,
        "expected_total_rows": EXPECTED_TOTAL_ROWS,
        "columns": list(columns),
        "unique_timestamp_dst_pairs": n_hours,
        "expected_unique_hours": EXPECTED_TIMESTAMPS,
        "unique_timestamps_without_dst": len(ts_only_counter),
        "dst_repeated_hours_count": len(dst_repeated_timestamps),
        "dst_repeated_timestamps": dst_repeated_timestamps,
        "missing_calendar_dates": missing_dates,
        "zones": dict(sorted(zone_counts.items())),
        "sources_raw_rows": dict(sorted(source_counts.items())),
        "archive_date_range": [
            min(ts for ts, s in zip(timestamps, sources) if s == "archive"),
            max(ts for ts, s in zip(timestamps, sources) if s == "archive"),
        ],
        "api_date_range": [
            min(ts for ts, s in zip(timestamps, sources) if s == "api"),
            max(ts for ts, s in zip(timestamps, sources) if s == "api"),
        ],
        "max_cross_zone_system_mw_spread": float(max_sys_spread),
        "cross_zone_source_mismatches": source_mismatch_count,
        "cross_zone_uri_mismatches": uri_mismatch_count,
        "raw_missing_weather_counts": dict(sorted(missing_raw_by_col.items())),
        "raw_missing_weather_by_split": dict(sorted(missing_raw_by_split.items())),
        "train_weather_impute_medians": {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in weather_impute_medians.items()},
        "uri_flag_zone_rows": uri_zone_rows,
        "uri_flag_system_hours": int(np.sum(uri_flags)),
        "uri_date_range": [min(uri_timestamps), max(uri_timestamps)] if uri_timestamps else [],
        "uri_peak_mw": round(float(np.max(uri_vals)), 2) if uri_vals.size else 0.0,
        "split_boundaries": {
            "train": ["2018-01-01 00:00:00", TRAIN_END],
            "val": [VAL_START, "2025-12-31 23:00:00"],
            "test": [TEST_START, timestamps[-1]],
        },
        "split_hour_counts": split_hour_counts,
        "split_load_stats_mw": split_load_stats,
        "overall_load_stats_mw": _summarize_load_dict(system_total_mw),
    }

    system_data: dict[str, Any] = {
        "timestamp": timestamps,
        "dst_flag": dst_flags,
        "source": sources,
        "uri_flag": uri_flags,
        "split": splits,
        "system_total_mw": system_total_mw,
        "zone_load_sum_mw": zone_load_sum_mw,
        "zone_loads": zone_loads_arr,
        "weather_mean": weather_mean_arr,
    }
    return system_data, audit_summary

numbers.operation: Group by (timestamp, DSTFlag) → verify max |sys_i - sys_j| == 0.0 → keep 1 system row/hour

beads.name: daily_profiles
beads.explains: Arrange each calendar day as 24 clock-hour loads, averaging fall-back hours and filling spring-forward hours.
beads.title: Build 24h Daily Profiles
beads.source:
def _build_daily_profiles(system_data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[date, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Aggregate the hourly system array into fixed 24-hour clock vectors [00..23] per day.

    Handling Daylight Saving Time (DST) transitions cleanly:
      - Normal days (3,211 days) have exactly 1 observation for each hour 0..23.
      - Fall-back DST days (9 days, 25 hours) have two 01:00 rows; averaging them aligns
        the fixed-width 24-hour matrix while flagging `is_dst_transition=True`.
      - Spring-forward DST days (9 days, 23 hours) skip 02:00; linear neighbor interpolation
        fills hour 02 ONLY inside the fixed-width 24-hour matrix (the exported hourly CSV
        preserves all 77,496 exact raw timestamps untouched).
    """
    # Group hourly array indices by ISO calendar date ("YYYY-MM-DD")
    grouped: dict[date, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
    for idx, ts in enumerate(system_data["timestamp"]):
        grouped[date.fromisoformat(ts[:10])].append(idx)

    daily: dict[date, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    sys_mw = system_data["system_total_mw"]
    uri_flags = system_data["uri_flag"]
    dst_flags = system_data["dst_flag"]
    weather = system_data["weather_mean"]

    for d, idxs in grouped.items():
        # Bucket indices by clock hour 0..23 within this calendar day
        hour_buckets: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
        for i in idxs:
            hr = int(system_data["timestamp"][i][11:13])
            hour_buckets[hr].append(i)

        load_24 = np.full(24, np.nan, dtype=np.float64)
        for hr, b_idxs in hour_buckets.items():
            # For normal hours len(b_idxs)==1; on fall-back 01:00 len(b_idxs)==2
            load_24[hr] = float(np.mean(sys_mw[b_idxs]))

        # Fill skipped 02:00 slot on spring-forward 23h days via adjacent-hour average
        is_dst_day = len(idxs) != 24 or any(bool(dst_flags[i]) for i in idxs)
        if np.isnan(load_24[2]) and not np.isnan(load_24[1]) and not np.isnan(load_24[3]):
            load_24[2] = 0.5 * (load_24[1] + load_24[3])
        if np.any(np.isnan(load_24)):
            valid_hrs = np.where(~np.isnan(load_24))[0]
            load_24 = np.interp(np.arange(24), valid_hrs, load_24[valid_hrs])

        # Precompute target-day weather summaries (mean/min/max across 4 vars) for optional upper-bound runs
        idx_arr = np.array(idxs, dtype=np.int64)
        weather_summary = np.array(
            [
                float(stat(weather[col][idx_arr]))
                for col in ("temp_f", "dwpt", "rhum", "wspd")
                for stat in (np.mean, np.min, np.max)
            ],
            dtype=np.float64,
        )

        daily[d] = {
            "load_24": load_24,
            "raw_hour_count": len(idxs),
            "is_dst_transition": is_dst_day,
            "is_uri": bool(np.any(uri_flags[idx_arr])),
            "split": system_data["split"][idxs[0]],
            "weather_summary": weather_summary,
        }
    return daily

numbers.operation: Bucket each date into [0..23] slots; average 25h fall-back 01:00; linearly fill 23h spring-forward 02:00

beads.name: day_ahead_features
beads.explains: Build the 67 causal inputs and 24 targets for each forecast day, scaled on training days only.
beads.title: Build 67 Inputs per Day
beads.source:
def split_and_prepare_features(system_data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build leakage-safe day-ahead 24h supervised matrices `(X_raw, X_scaled, Y)`.

    Forecast Issuance Protocol (Proposal Section 4.1):
      Standing at the end of origin day `d` (23:00), predict the 24 hourly loads of
      tomorrow `target_d = d + 1`. Only information observed on or before day `d` plus
      deterministic calendar features of `d + 1` enters `X_raw`:
        1. `lag_1d` (24 features): Today's (`origin_d`) 24 hourly loads.
        2. `lag_7d` (24 features): Same weekday one week ago (`target_d - 7d == origin_d - 6d`).
        3. `past_2to6d_summary` (4 features): Mean, std, min, max across available days in `[d-5..d-1]`.
        4. `roll_7d_summary` (4 features): Mean, std, min, max across available days in `[d-6..d]`.
        5. `calendar` (11 features): Cyclical month, day-of-week one-hot, weekend, DST transition.

    Leakage Controls:
      - Missing calendar date `2026-10-30` is handled by checking exact `date` dictionary keys
        instead of blind array indexing, preventing shifted lag alignment.
      - Target-day observed weather is NEVER included in `X_raw`/`X_scaled`; it is isolated in
        `upper_bound_weather_only` for optional non-causal upper-bound ablation checks only.
      - Feature standardization (`scaler_mean`, `scaler_std`) is fit strictly on `train` days.
    """
    daily = _build_daily_profiles(system_data)
    sorted_dates = sorted(daily.keys())

    x_rows: list[np.ndarray] = []
    y_rows: list[np.ndarray] = []
    ub_weather_rows: list[np.ndarray] = []
    origin_dates: list[str] = []
    target_dates: list[str] = []
    sample_splits: list[str] = []
    uri_masks: list[bool] = []
    dst_masks: list[bool] = []

    for origin_d in sorted_dates:
        target_d = origin_d + timedelta(days=1)
        # Same weekday 7 days before target_d corresponds to (origin_d - 6 days)
        lag7_d = target_d - timedelta(days=7)

        # Skip boundaries where tomorrow (`target_d`) or the 7-day baseline (`lag7_d`) is absent
        # (e.g., first 6 days of Jan 2018, or adjacent to missing date 2026-10-30).
        if target_d not in daily or lag7_d not in daily:
            continue

        # Collect days [d-5 .. d-1] (robust to a single missing intermediate day)
        past_2to6_loads = [
            daily[origin_d - timedelta(days=k)]["load_24"]
            for k in range(1, 6)
            if (origin_d - timedelta(days=k)) in daily
        ]
        if not past_2to6_loads:
            continue

        # Collect the full trailing 7-day window [d-6 .. d] available at forecast issuance
        roll_7d_loads = [
            daily[origin_d - timedelta(days=k)]["load_24"]
            for k in range(0, 7)
            if (origin_d - timedelta(days=k)) in daily
        ]
        lag_1d_vec = daily[origin_d]["load_24"]
        lag_7d_vec = daily[lag7_d]["load_24"]
        summary_2to6 = _four_stat_vec(np.concatenate(past_2to6_loads))
        summary_7d = _four_stat_vec(np.concatenate(roll_7d_loads))
        cal_vec = _calendar_features(target_d, daily[target_d]["is_dst_transition"])

        # Concatenate all 67 causal predictors into one row vector for origin_d -> target_d
        feat_vec = np.concatenate([lag_1d_vec, lag_7d_vec, summary_2to6, summary_7d, cal_vec])
        x_rows.append(feat_vec)
        y_rows.append(daily[target_d]["load_24"])
        ub_weather_rows.append(daily[target_d]["weather_summary"])
        origin_dates.append(origin_d.isoformat())
        target_dates.append(target_d.isoformat())
        # Assign sample split according to the target day being predicted
        sample_splits.append(daily[target_d]["split"])
        uri_masks.append(daily[target_d]["is_uri"] or daily[origin_d]["is_uri"])
        dst_masks.append(daily[target_d]["is_dst_transition"])

    X_raw = np.vstack(x_rows)
    Y = np.vstack(y_rows)
    upper_bound_weather_only = np.vstack(ub_weather_rows)
    splits_arr = np.array(sample_splits)

    # Leakage Control #2: Compute mean & std strictly from `train` rows (2018-2023),
    # guarding near-zero-variance features with a 1.0 denominator before scaling all splits.
    train_idx = splits_arr == "train"
    scaler_mean = np.mean(X_raw[train_idx], axis=0)
    scaler_std = np.std(X_raw[train_idx], axis=0)
    scaler_std = np.where(scaler_std < 1e-8, 1.0, scaler_std)
    X_scaled = (X_raw - scaler_mean) / scaler_std

    return {
        "feature_names": np.array(get_day_ahead_feature_names()),
        "X_raw": X_raw,
        "X_scaled": X_scaled,
        "Y": Y,
        "upper_bound_weather_only": upper_bound_weather_only,
        "scaler_mean": scaler_mean,
        "scaler_std": scaler_std,
        "origin_dates": np.array(origin_dates),
        "target_dates": np.array(target_dates),
        "splits": splits_arr,
        "uri_mask": np.array(uri_masks, dtype=bool),
        "dst_mask": np.array(dst_masks, dtype=bool),
    }

      tokens=("SVR", "6,000", "subsampling", "kernel"),
      explains="Take 6,000 training hours at evenly spaced positions to keep the kernel fit tractable.")
def svr_sample(ex: HourlyExamples, max_samples: int = MAX_SAMPLES) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    train = ex.split("train")
    x, y = ex.x[train], ex.y[train]
    if len(x) <= max_samples:
        return x, y
    positions = np.linspace(0, len(x) - 1, max_samples, dtype=int)
    return x[positions], y[positions]

      explains="Try every C, epsilon and gamma in the grid and keep the lowest validation MAE.")
def svr_search(ex: HourlyExamples, grid=GRID) -> tuple[TransformedTargetRegressor, dict, list[dict]]:
    x, y = svr_sample(ex)
    val = ex.split("val")
    results, best, best_params, best_mae = [], None, None, float("inf")
    for params in ParameterGrid(grid):
        model = svr_fit(x, y, **params)
        score = errors(ex.y[val], model.predict(ex.x[val]))
        results.append({**params, **score})
        if score["mae_mw"] < best_mae:
            best, best_params, best_mae = model, params, score["mae_mw"]
    return best, best_params, results

beads.name: armijo_update
beads.explains: One full-batch gradient step; halve the step until the Armijo sufficient-decrease test passes.
beads.title: Full-Batch Armijo FFN Step
beads.source:
@bead("armijo_update", strand="ffn", after=("ffn_network", "ffn_targets"),
      title="Full-Batch Armijo FFN Step",
      io=("full batch grad", "1 step + line search"),
      tokens=("Armijo", "full-batch", "backtracking", "FFN", "2,083.21"),
      explains="One full-batch gradient step; halve the step until the Armijo sufficient-decrease test passes.")
def armijo_update(model: nn.Module, train_x: torch.Tensor, train_y: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[float, int]:
    params = list(model.parameters())
    model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    loss = _loss(model(train_x), train_y)
    loss.backward()
    with torch.no_grad():
        start = parameters_to_vector(params)
        grad = parameters_to_vector([p.grad for p in params])
        squared_norm = grad.square().sum().item()
        base_loss = loss.item()
        step = ARMIJO["initial_step"]
        for evaluations in range(1, ARMIJO["max_search"] + 1):
            vector_to_parameters(start - step * grad, params)
            if _loss(model(train_x), train_y).item() <= base_loss - ARMIJO["sufficient_decrease"] * step * squared_norm:
                return step, evaluations
            step *= ARMIJO["shrink"]
        vector_to_parameters(start, params)
    raise RuntimeError("Armijo line search exhausted the trial steps.")

numbers.operation: 1 full-batch gradient + backtracking line search on MSE

beads.name: sgd_pass
beads.explains: One shuffled pass over the training days in mini-batches of 32, one SGD step per batch.

beads.source:
@bead("sgd_pass", strand="ffn", after=("ffn_network", "ffn_targets"),
      title="Mini-Batch SGD Epoch",
      io=("shuffled batches of 32", "69 SGD steps/pass"),
      tokens=("mini-batch", "SGD", "batch 32", "0.03", "1,786.59"),
      explains="One shuffled pass over the training days in mini-batches of 32, one SGD step per batch.")
def sgd_pass(model, optimizer, generator, train_x, train_y, batch_size: int = BATCH_SIZE) -> int:
    order = torch.randperm(len(train_x), generator=generator)
    for batch in order.split(batch_size):
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        _loss(model(train_x[batch]), train_y[batch]).backward()
        optimizer.step()
    return (len(order) + batch_size - 1) // batch_size

beads.name: ffn_train
beads.explains: Run 100 passes with one optimizer and keep the weights with the lowest validation MAE.
beads.title: Train FFN for 100 Passes
beads.source:
@bead("ffn_train", strand="ffn", after=("armijo_update", "sgd_pass"),
      title="Train FFN for 100 Passes",
      io=("100 passes", "best val checkpoint"),
      tokens=("100 passes", "SGD vs Armijo", "1,777.38", "2,033.09", "6,900 grads"),
      explains="Run 100 passes with one optimizer and keep the weights with the lowest validation MAE.")
def ffn_train(p: FFNProblem, method: str, learning_rate: float | None, starting_model: nn.Module,
              shuffle_seed: int = SEED, passes: int = PASSES) -> dict:
    model = copy.deepcopy(starting_model)
    optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate) if learning_rate is not None else None
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(shuffle_seed)
    train_x, train_y, _ = p.part("train")
    started = perf_counter()
    steps, gradients, search_evals, optimizer_seconds = [], 0, 0, 0.0
    best_mae, best_pass, best_state = float("inf"), None, None
    for epoch in range(passes + 1):
        step = None
        if epoch:
            update_start = perf_counter()
            if optimizer is None:
                step, evaluations = armijo_update(model, train_x, train_y)
                gradients += 1
                search_evals += evaluations
            else:
                gradients += sgd_pass(model, optimizer, generator, train_x, train_y)
            optimizer_seconds += perf_counter() - update_start
        diagnostics = _monitor(model, p)
        steps.append({"method": method, "pass": epoch, "optimizer_seconds": optimizer_seconds,
                      "gradient_evaluations": gradients, "line_search_evaluations": search_evals,
                      "armijo_step": step, **diagnostics})
        if diagnostics["validation_mae_mw"] < best_mae:
            best_mae, best_pass = diagnostics["validation_mae_mw"], epoch
            best_state = copy.deepcopy(model.state_dict())
    summary = {"method": method, "learning_rate": learning_rate, "best_pass": best_pass,
               "validation_mae_mw": best_mae, "optimizer_seconds": optimizer_seconds,
               "run_seconds": perf_counter() - started, "gradient_evaluations": gradients,
               "line_search_evaluations": search_evals}
    return {"summary": summary, "history": pd.DataFrame(steps), "weights": best_state}

def lstm_calendar(grid: DayGrid) -> Calendar:
    days = grid.days
    holidays = USFederalHolidayCalendar().holidays(days.min(), days.max())
    dow = days.day_of_week.to_numpy()
    offday = ((dow >= 5) | days.isin(holidays)).astype(float)
    dow_s, dow_c = _cyc(dow, 7)
    doy_s, doy_c = _cyc(days.day_of_year.to_numpy(), 365.25)
    return Calendar(dow, offday, doy_s, doy_c, np.column_stack([dow_s, dow_c, offday, doy_s, doy_c]))

beads.title: 14-Day Normalized Windows
beads.source:
@bead("lstm_samples", strand="lstm", after=("lstm_calendar",),
      title="14-Day Normalized Windows",
      io=("14-day window", "relative load / 7d mean"),
      tokens=("14-day lookback", "7-day mean", "level normalization", "LSTM", "sequence"),
      explains="For each target day, stack the previous 14 days divided by the trailing 7-day mean load.")
def lstm_samples(grid: DayGrid, cal: Calendar, lookback: int, level_days: int = 7) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    L = grid.load
    rows = np.array([t for t in range(max(lookback, level_days), len(L)) if grid.target_ok[t]])
    level = np.array([L[t - level_days:t].mean() for t in rows])
    seq_load = np.stack([L[t - lookback:t] for t in rows]) / level[:, None, None]
    static = np.column_stack([np.eye(7)[cal.dow[rows]], cal.offday[rows], cal.doy_s[rows], cal.doy_c[rows],
                              np.log(level)])
    return dict(rows=rows, level=level, seq_load=seq_load,
                seq_cal=np.stack([cal.day_cal[t - lookback:t] for t in rows]),
                static=static, y_rel=L[rows] / level[:, None], split=grid.split[rows],
                uri=np.array([grid.uri[t - lookback:t + 1].any() for t in rows]))

beads.name: lstm_train
beads.explains: Nesterov SGD on shuffled batches with gradient clipping, a plateau schedule and early stopping.
beads.title: Nesterov SGD LSTM Training
beads.source:
@bead("lstm_train", strand="lstm", after=("lstm_network",),
      title="Nesterov SGD LSTM Training",
      io=("Nesterov SGD lr=0.03", "best early-stop weights"),
      tokens=("Nesterov", "SGD", "early stopping", "gradient clip", "LR schedule"),
      explains="Nesterov SGD on shuffled batches with gradient clipping, a plateau schedule and early stopping.")
def lstm_train(cfg: dict, data: dict, grid: DayGrid, seed: int = 42, verbose: bool = False):
    cfg = {**CONFIG, **cfg}
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    tr, va = data["tensors"]["train"], data["tensors"]["val"]
    model = lstm_network(data, cfg)
    opt = make_optimizer(cfg, model.parameters())
    sched = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.ReduceLROnPlateau(opt, factor=cfg["lr_factor"], patience=cfg["lr_patience"])
    loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(*tr), batch_size=cfg["batch"], shuffle=True,
                        generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed))
    loss_fn = nn.MSELoss()
    S, sc, va_rows = data["S"], data["scaler"], data["masks"]["val"]
    hist = {k: [] for k in ["epoch", "train_obj", "val_loss", "val_mae_mw", "grad_norm", "lr", "time"]}
    best, best_state, wait, t0 = np.inf, None, 0, time.perf_counter()
    for epoch in range(1, cfg["max_epochs"] + 1):
        model.train()
        gnorms = []
        for xb, sb, yb in loader:
            opt.zero_grad()
            loss = loss_fn(model(xb, sb), yb)
            loss.backward()
            gnorms.append(float(nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), cfg["clip"])))
            opt.step()
        p_tr, p_va = predict_std(model, tr[0], tr[1]), predict_std(model, va[0], va[1])
        train_obj = float(((p_tr - tr[2].numpy()) ** 2).mean())
        val_loss = float(((p_va - va[2].numpy()) ** 2).mean())
        val_mae = np.abs(sc.to_mw(p_va, S["level"][va_rows]) - grid.load[S["rows"][va_rows]]).mean()
        sched.step(val_loss)
        for k, v in zip(hist, [epoch, train_obj, val_loss, val_mae, np.mean(gnorms),
                               opt.param_groups[0]["lr"], time.perf_counter() - t0]):
            hist[k].append(v)
        if verbose and (epoch % 20 == 0 or epoch == 1):
            print(f"ep {epoch:3d} train {train_obj:.4f} val {val_loss:.4f} valMAE {val_mae:7.0f} MW")
        if val_loss < best - 1e-5:
            best, best_state, wait = val_loss, copy.deepcopy(model.state_dict()), 0
        else:
            wait += 1
            if wait >= cfg["patience"]:
                break
    model.load_state_dict(best_state)
    hist = pd.DataFrame(hist)
    hist.attrs["best_epoch"] = int(hist.loc[hist.val_loss.idxmin(), "epoch"])
    hist.attrs["train_seconds"] = hist["time"].iloc[-1]
    return model, hist

numbers.operation: Train up to 200 epochs with ReduceLROnPlateau(0.5, 8) and patience=25 early stopping

beads.title: Load Saved Seed Checkpoints
beads.source:
@bead("lstm_load_weights", strand="lstm", after=("lstm_network",),
      title="Load Saved Seed Checkpoints",
      io=("lstm_seed*.pt", "restored LSTMForecaster"),
      tokens=("weights", "checkpoints", "seed 42", "seed 7", "seed 2026"),
      explains="Load the saved weights of one trained seed instead of retraining.")
def lstm_load_weights(data: dict, seed: int, cfg: dict = CONFIG, directory: Path = WEIGHTS_DIR) -> LSTMForecaster:
    model = lstm_network(data, cfg)
    model.load_state_dict(torch.load(directory / f"lstm_seed{seed}.pt", map_location="cpu", weights_only=True))
    return model
